text.title: Humpback whale
text.menu_sub: Swim in the open sea and come up to breathe.
text.menu_wild: Breathe at the top and rest near it.
text.intro: Swim in the open sea. Come up to the top to breathe. Rest near the top of the water.
text.hungry: You hardly eat on the reef, living on your fat. If you get hungry, gulp small fish.
text.no_food: No small fish within reach. Swim on and look again.
text.night_hint: Rest near the top of the water.
text.sheltered: You can rest here in the water.
text.about_looks: A very big blue-grey whale with a pale belly and very long white flippers. It is about 14 metres long.
text.about_food: Krill and small schooling fish in cold seas. On the warm reef it hardly eats and lives on its fat.
text.about_home: Swims in the open sea and near reefs. It rests near the top of the water.
text.about_winter: In the southern winter it swims from cold feeding waters near Antarctica to warm waters like the reef.
text.about_young: Calves are born in warm shallow water in the southern winter, around June to September. They stay close to their mothers.
text.about_fact: Its long flippers are about one-third of its body. Each whale has its own black and white pattern underneath its tail.
text.rain_start: It's raining on the sea. A whale doesn't mind.
text.safe_tag: Tag, you got it! In Safe mode a whale never goes hungry.
text.bite: A huge whale gulped right next to you! Swim away!
text.caught_you: A whale swallowed you in a mouthful of water.

year.shelter: Rests near the top of the water. Swims in the open sea and near reefs.
year.young: Calves are born in warm shallow water in winter. They stay close to their mothers.

food.summer: Hardly eats on the reef; lives on its blubber.
food.autumn: Hardly eats on the reef; lives on its blubber.

year.notes: On the Great Barrier Reef from June to November to have calves; feeds on krill in Antarctica the rest of the year.
